elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Retained mutual language, untouched by the edit.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 now reads "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" — paid-or-payable basis, 12-month window anchored to the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor all present. The deliberate lowercase "fees" plus "under this Agreement and all Order Forms" escapes the illusory defined "Fees" (= one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee).

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.2 (retained): "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "'Excluded Claims' means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations"; § 21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 Excluded Claims expressly includes "data-protection, or security obligations", which sit outside both the cap (§ 21.1) and the consequential-damages exclusion (§ 21.2).
§ 21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is within the Excluded Claims definition carved out of § 21.1.
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
§ 21.3: "or fraud" within Excluded Claims, carved out of the § 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 retains only "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." "Fees" is defined at §§ 1.5–1.6 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, and the sentence is further narrowed to "undisputed" amounts for "conforming" Services — a narrow subset, not Customer's payment obligations as a whole.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 retained sentence: "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims"; the operative cap runs to "each Party's total aggregate liability".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Edited § 21.1: "the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim". The edit removes the two defects that made the prior measure illusory (capital-F "Fees" = USD 12,000 one-time Implementation Fee; "under the first Order Form").
§ 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"; § 21.1 caps liability "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" is an Excluded Claim.
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" are Excluded Claims outside the § 21.1 cap.
§ 21.3: "wilful misconduct" expressly listed among Excluded Claims.

reasons: Deviation classification is correct: as drafted the cap measured "Fees" (defined at §§ 1.5–1.6 as a one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) "under the first Order Form", which is far below 6 months' fees and sits in walk-away territory. The single operation cures that.
Fallback is position-complete: mutuality, the 12-month fee basis, and the indemnity/confidentiality/gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct carve-outs are all present in operative language.

Preferred is not complete. The only gap is the payment carve-out: § 21.3 excludes from "damages" only "undisputed Fees for conforming Services", and "Fees" remains the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee. To reach preferred, amend that sentence to read, e.g., "Customer's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement is not damages and is not limited by this Section." The drafter's decision to leave it is defensible commercially but must not be described as preferred-complete.

Minimality fails on the USD 1,000,000 floor. The declared target is the fallback, whose only numeric requirement is a cap "based on 12 months of fees"; "the greater of ... and (b) USD 1,000,000" exceeds that threshold with no stated necessity (and, because the cap is mutual, it also raises Customer's own exposure floor). Either delete "the greater of" and limb (b) to sit cleanly at the fallback, or keep the floor and pursue the full preferred level by also fixing the § 21.3 payment sentence.

Minor drafting point (not a failure): the edit relies on lowercase "fees" to escape the capital-F defined term while §§ 1.5–1.6 are left intact. That is the right minimal move for the rest of the contract, but consider adding "(regardless of the definition of 'Fees' in Section 1.5)" or amending § 1.5 if Vendor argues the defined term controls.

Intent is preserved: § 21.2's mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the direct-damages carve-in for data restoration and incident response, and the § 21.3 Excluded Claims definition are untouched; no cross-reference is left dangling and "Fees" remains defined for the payment and § 21.3 sentences.
